comparison: Both strongly support the functional characterization (C2, C27-C29, C31). OpenEval emphasizes adequate sample size and kinetic validation; peer reviewers confirm successful functional testing with no concerns raised. OpenEval also covers C30, C32 which peer review includes.

Both support the cryo-EM structural determination (C3, C37-C39). OpenEval notes adequate resolution and reasonable state assignments with caveats about functional correspondence. Peer review confirms comprehensive structural data across states. OpenEval addresses C33-C34 separately while peer review includes C40-C41 about particle orientations.

OpenEval supports the desensitization gate identification (C4-C5, C48-C49, C52-C55, C60) based on structural data and prior mutagenesis. Peer review expresses uncertainty, with Reviewer 2 noting 'limited functional data' and concern that structures only provide 'snapshots.' This represents a key disagreement about the strength of evidence for functional state assignments.

Strong agreement on liposome vs. nanodisc structural comparisons (C6-C7, C83-C85, C87, C90, C92-C96). Both recognize the finding that TMD is more loosely packed in liposomes and that large nanodiscs deviate most. Editor and reviewers describe comparison as 'convincing' and 'important.'

Complete agreement on ELIC's rim localization in nanodiscs (C8, C68-C69, C71-C72, C105). Both accept the MSP density evidence from cryo-EM data. Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges this finding contradicted original hypotheses. OpenEval does not address C9 which peer review includes.

Both support the observations about MSP effects on protein dynamics (C73, C75-C78, C88). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of local resolution and M4 visibility; peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'thorough' structural analysis. Peer review includes C74 which OpenEval addresses separately in R26.

Perfect claim overlap (C62-C67) and complete agreement. Both support the lipid density observations and conclusion that ELIC determines lipid interactions similarly in liposomes and nanodiscs. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect claim overlap (C79-C82) and complete agreement. Both support the observation of protein association in large nanodiscs from 2D class averages. Both acknowledge the speculation about association promotion is appropriately qualified and requires further validation.

Both express uncertainty about particle orientation assignments (C40-C41). OpenEval notes limitations in distinguishing inward/outward-facing particles and resulting uncertainty. Peer review accepts the structural data as comprehensive but doesn't specifically highlight orientation concerns in the same way.

OpenEval supports the reconstitution methodology (C20-C24) as well-described and validated. Peer review expresses uncertainty, with Reviewer 3 wanting 'greater details' about biochemistry and concern about preservation of native structure during the reconstitution process. Peer review also addresses C25-C26 which OpenEval covers in R25.

Both support conclusions about M4 structural differences and nanodisc effects (C113-C117). OpenEval emphasizes structural evidence and argues liposomes are necessary. Peer reviewers accept the structural observations and acknowledge MSP effects on functional states, though with some uncertainty about the strength of 'necessity' claims.

OpenEval supports conformational changes across states (C45-C47, C113-C114) based on structural comparisons. Peer review addresses overlapping claims about M4 movements (C113-C114) and accepts these as part of the convincing comparative analysis.

Both support ELIC5 characterization (C30, C32). OpenEval cites prior work and confirms with functional data. Peer review includes these claims in broader functional validation without specific concerns.

OpenEval supports the F247 dual conformation modeling (C50-C51) as appropriate given density heterogeneity. Peer review includes these claims but expresses broader uncertainty about functional state assignments based on structural snapshots.

OpenEval supports lipid composition choice (C25-C26) based on citations and bacterial membrane composition. Peer review includes these in broader methodological concerns, wanting more biochemical details about the reconstitution process.

OpenEval supports citation context (C70, C74) for interpreting MSP effects. Peer review accepts the MSP-related structural observations (C74 included) as part of thorough analysis without specifically highlighting the citation.

OpenEval supports state assignments (C33-C34) with caveats about functional correspondence. Peer review expresses uncertainty about whether liposomes are 'necessary' for native structure, with Reviewer 2's concern about limited functional validation creating doubt about strong interpretive claims.

OpenEval supports integration of functional and structural data (C99-C103, including C102). Peer review's uncertainty about functional state determination (C102 context) reflects concern that structural snapshots alone are insufficient despite the integrated approach.

OpenEval supports resolution of prior uncertainty (C99-C101). Peer review acknowledges liposomes may be more representative but expresses uncertainty about the strength of this conclusion given limited functional validation.

OpenEval supports necessity of liposome structures (C115-C118) based on M4 differences. Peer review accepts structural differences but expresses uncertainty about 'necessity' claim, viewing it as extending beyond what structural comparisons alone establish.
OpenEval supports background context claims (C1, C10-C16) about pLGICs and membrane proteins based on literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.
OpenEval supports prior work context (C17-C19, C97) about nanodiscs and notes current work challenges predictions. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific contextual claims.
OpenEval supports literature context (C56-C59, C61) about desensitization gates in pLGICs. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.

OpenEval supports expected pLGIC architectural features (C42-C44) as confirming proper structure. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these confirmatory observations.
OpenEval supports observation that nanodisc effects are more pronounced in agonist-bound states (C89). No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific comparative finding.

OpenEval supports generalization to other membrane proteins (C109-C110) based on recent literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this broader implication.
